ROLE: Create the listening TCP socket: SOCK_NONBLOCK | SOCK_CLOEXEC, SO_REUSEADDR, bind to INADDR_ANY on the requested port and listen, closing the descriptor on every failure path.

STRUCT.NAME: struct sockaddr_in
STRUCT.ROLE: IPv4 bind address with the requested port

FUNC.NAME: socket
FUNC.ROLE: create the listening descriptor with SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_NONBLOCK | SOCK_CLOEXEC

FUNC.NAME: setsockopt
FUNC.ROLE: enable SO_REUSEADDR so a restarting broker can rebind quickly

FUNC.NAME: bind
FUNC.ROLE: reserve the local port on all interfaces

FUNC.NAME: listen
FUNC.ROLE: mark the socket as accepting connections

FUNC.NAME: close
FUNC.ROLE: release the descriptor on a failed setup

FUNC.NAME: htons
FUNC.ROLE: convert the port to network byte order

FUNC.NAME: htonl
FUNC.ROLE: convert INADDR_ANY (all local addresses) to network byte order

VAR.NAME: SOCK_STREAM
VAR.ROLE: TCP stream socket type, combined with the mode flags

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: socket
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int socket(int domain, int type, int protocol)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: a new nonblocking close-on-exec descriptor >= 0, or -1 with errno set
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the returned descriptor is owned by this function until it is returned to the caller; on later failure it is closed here
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 means no descriptor exists and this function returns -1 immediately

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: setsockopt
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int setsockopt(int fd, int level, int optname, const void *optval, socklen_t optlen)
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 means the socket cannot be configured; this function closes the descriptor and returns -1 so the caller aborts startup

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: bind
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: int bind(int fd, const struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addrlen)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 when the port was reserved (EADDRINUSE is the usual failure), -1 with errno set
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 means the port is unusable; this function closes the descriptor and returns -1 so main can report the bind error

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: listen
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 means the socket cannot accept; this function closes the descriptor and returns -1

LOGIC.INPUT: port: TCP port in host byte order (the CLI passes 1..65535; 0 is allowed so tests can ask the kernel for an ephemeral port). backlog: listen backlog, normally 128.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If backlog < 1 return -1 with errno = EINVAL (a listen backlog must be positive). 2) fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_NONBLOCK | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0); if fd < 0 return -1 with errno unchanged from socket. The mode flags are requested at creation time, so the listener is nonblocking and close-on-exec without any fcntl fallback. 3) int one = 1; if setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &one, sizeof one) != 0 { saved = errno; close(fd); errno = saved; return -1; }. 4) memset(&addr, 0, sizeof addr); addr.sin_family = AF_INET; addr.sin_port = htons(port); addr.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_ANY); if bind(fd, (const struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof addr) != 0 { saved = errno; close(fd); errno = saved; return -1; }. 5) if listen(fd, backlog) != 0 { saved = errno; close(fd); errno = saved; return -1; }. 6) Return fd. The descriptor is returned open, nonblocking and close-on-exec; ownership transfers to the caller, which must close it with net_close_fd.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: A listening descriptor >= 0 on success; -1 with errno set (EINVAL for a nonpositive backlog, otherwise the errno of the failing call) on failure. No descriptor is leaked on any failure path: every error after a successful socket() closes the descriptor first while preserving errno. The listener's readiness mask is EPOLLIN only; it is registered by loop_add_listener.
INVARIANTS_USED: descriptor modes are established at creation time (SOCK_NONBLOCK | SOCK_CLOEXEC) and never depend on process umask or on a listener
the broker binds INADDR_ANY so any local address is reachable
SO_REUSEADDR avoids a TIME_WAIT bind failure on restart
the caller owns the returned descriptor and closes it exactly once
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: No other process holds the requested port (or SO_REUSEADDR makes it rebindable).
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: On success one owned listening descriptor exists and no other resource; on failure no descriptor from this call remains open.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Safe to call from one thread; the returned descriptor is independent of other sockets.

EXPECT.note: bind used htons(0) so the kernel picked the port; this is how tests obtain a free port
SO_REUSEADDR allows the rebind; the first descriptor was closed so no leak
checked before socket() so no descriptor is created

calls: hold port P with a first listener
net_listen(P, 128) with SO_REUSEADDR but an active listener
